questions.question:
Under the Digital Agriculture Mission launched in 2024, which of the following is/are among the foundational registries of AgriStack?

 1. Farmers’ Registry

 2. Village Panchayat Audit Database

 3. Crop Sown Registry
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 3 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Digital Agriculture Mission, launched by the Government of India, aims to leverage **technology and data-driven solutions** to transform the agricultural sector.
 
• As part of the initiative, **AgriStack** was conceptualized to create a unified platform for farmers, combining various digital services and solutions.
 
• The foundational registries under AgriStack include the **Farmers' Registry** and the **Crop Sown Registry**, which are essential for tracking farmer identities and land usage.
 
• The inclusion of the **Village Panchayat Audit Database** is not part of the foundational registries under AgriStack.
 
• These registries enable better targeting of government schemes, efficient resource allocation, and streamlined service delivery to farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Digital Agriculture Mission:**

 
 
• Launched in 2021, this mission focuses on the adoption of emerging technologies like artificial intelligence, blockchain, and IoT in agriculture.
 
• It aims to improve productivity, increase farmers' income, and promote sustainable agricultural practices.
 
 
 
• **AgriStack:**
 
 
• AgriStack is a collection of digital databases and tools that provide comprehensive information about India's agricultural sector.
 
• It includes foundational datasets like land records, crop patterns, weather data, and farmer profiles.
 
• AgriStack helps in better implementation of schemes like PM-KISAN, soil health card, and crop insurance.
 
 
 
• **Farmers' Registry:**
 
 
• This registry is a centralized database of farmers, including their demographic and landholding details.
 
• It ensures that only eligible farmers receive the benefits of government schemes.
 
 
 
• **Crop Sown Registry:**
 
 
• This registry tracks the crops grown by farmers on their lands, enabling better planning for procurement and distribution.
 
• It also aids in estimating agricultural outputs and ensuring food security.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the ‘One Nation, One Permit’ scheme proposed by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways?

options.text: . Ease of transport for inter-state freight vehicles

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ease of transport for inter-state freight vehicles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'One Nation, One Permit' scheme aims to simplify the movement of **inter-state freight vehicles** in India.
 
• This initiative seeks to address logistical challenges and reduce the administrative burden of acquiring multiple permits for cross-border transportation.
 
• It would enable seamless movement of goods across Indian states, **enhancing economic efficiency and reducing transportation costs.**
 
• By eliminating the need for separate state permits, the scheme would contribute to **streamlining the supply chain network** and improving ease of doing business.
 
• The scheme is part of the broader reforms under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to modernize India's freight transportation system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inter-State Freight Transportation:**

 
 
• It involves the movement of goods across state boundaries within a country.
 
• Traditionally, separate permits were required in India for each state, leading to delays and higher costs.
 
 
 
• **Logistics Performance Index (LPI):**
 
 
• This is a World Bank index that ranks countries based on the efficiency of their logistics and supply chain networks.
 
• India has been focusing on improving its LPI ranking through reforms like 'One Nation, One Permit.'
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact of Streamlined Logistics:**
 
 
• Efficient logistics reduce transportation costs, which can lead to lower prices for consumers.
 
• It also boosts GDP by facilitating faster and more reliable trade.
 
 
 
• **Government Digital Initiatives:**
 
 
• Other similar initiatives include the GST e-way bill system, which aims to simplify goods movement tracking.
 
• Digital platforms and automation are being integrated to reduce manual intervention in freight management.

questions.question: As per the NFHS-5 (2019-21), what is the approximate percentage of households in India with access to improved sanitation facilities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**70%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the **National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5)** conducted during 2019-21, **approximately 70% of households in India have access to improved sanitation facilities.**
 
• Improved sanitation facilities refer to access to toilets that hygienically separate human excreta from human contact, such as flush toilets or pit latrines.
 
• The NFHS-5 data reflects a significant improvement compared to previous NFHS surveys, highlighting progress in India's sanitation infrastructure.
 
• **Government initiatives such as Swachh Bharat Mission** have been instrumental in driving improved sanitation coverage across the country.
 
• Rural areas have witnessed substantial growth in sanitation facilities, narrowing the gap with urban areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Improved Sanitation Facilities:**

 
 
• Defined as facilities that hygienically separate human excreta from human contact.
 
• Examples include flush/pour flush toilets, ventilated improved pit latrines, and composting toilets.
 
• These facilities contribute to better public health and reduced waterborne diseases.
 
 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission:**
 
 
• Launched in 2014 by the Government of India to eliminate open defecation and improve sanitation.
 
• Focused on constructing toilets, waste management, and raising awareness about hygiene.
 
• Played a key role in increasing access to improved sanitation facilities.
 
 
 
• **NFHS-5 Survey:**
 
 
• Conducted by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India.
 
• A comprehensive survey covering health, nutrition, and population indicators.
 
• Provides critical data for policymaking and tracking national progress.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Improved Sanitation:**
 
 
• Reduces the prevalence of waterborne diseases like diarrhea and cholera.
 
• Improves overall public health and productivity.
 
• Enhances environmental sustainability by reducing pollution.

questions.question: In December 2024, PM Modi made a historic visit to which Gulf country, marking the first such visit by an Indian Prime Minister in 43 years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuwait**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In **December 2024**, PM Narendra Modi visited **Kuwait**, marking the first visit by an Indian Prime Minister to the country in** 43 years**.
 
• The visit was a significant milestone in strengthening **India-Kuwait bilateral relations**.
 
• Kuwait is a key partner for India in the Gulf region, especially in terms of energy cooperation and trade.
 
• India and Kuwait have deep historical, cultural, and economic ties, with over **1 million Indians residing in Kuwait** as part of the Indian diaspora.
 
• PM Modi’s visit aimed to enhance **economic, strategic, and cultural cooperation** between the two nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India-Kuwait Relations:**

 
 
• Kuwait is a significant supplier of crude oil to India, making it an important partner in India’s energy security.
 
• The Indian diaspora in Kuwait plays a crucial role in the development of Kuwait's economy and sends back significant remittances to India.
 
• India and Kuwait have agreements covering defense, investment, and cultural exchanges.
 
 
 
• **Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC):**
 
 
• Kuwait is a member of the GCC, a regional intergovernmental political and economic union comprising six Gulf countries.
 
• India holds strong ties with GCC nations, and Kuwait is an essential part of this framework.
 
 
 
• **Indian Diaspora in Kuwait:**
 
 
• There are over 1 million Indians living in Kuwait, constituting the largest expatriate community in the country.
 
• The diaspora contributes significantly to the bilateral relationship, including through remittances and cultural exchanges.
 
 
 
• **Historical Visits:**
 
 
• The last visit by an Indian Prime Minister to Kuwait was made by PM Indira Gandhi in 1981.
 
• PM Modi’s visit in 2024 marked the resumption of high-level engagements between the two nations after four decades.

questions.question: When and where is the second part of the Fifth Session (INC-5.2) of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC) on plastic pollution scheduled to take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**August 2025 in Geneva, Switzerland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The second part of the Fifth Session (INC-5.2) of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC) on plastic pollution is scheduled to take place in **August 2025 in Geneva, Switzerland**.
 
• The INC sessions are organized by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) to negotiate a legally binding treaty addressing **plastic pollution on a global scale**.
 
• The Fifth Session (INC-5) is divided into two parts to allow for comprehensive discussions and consensus-building among the participating nations.
 
• The location, Geneva, Switzerland, is significant as it is home to numerous international organizations, including UNEP offices, making it a hub for global environmental negotiations.
 
• INC sessions aim to address crucial aspects such as plastic production, consumption, waste management, and environmental impact reduction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plastic Pollution**

 
 
• Plastic pollution refers to the accumulation of plastic products and particles in the environment, adversely affecting wildlife, habitats, and humans.
 
• Nearly 400 million tonnes of plastic are produced annually, with a significant portion ending up as waste in oceans and ecosystems.
 
• The United Nations has recognized plastic pollution as a pressing global environmental challenge.
 
 
 
• **Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC)**
 
 
• The INC was established following the United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA) resolution in March 2022.
 
• The committee is tasked with developing an international legally binding instrument to end plastic pollution.
 
• Its negotiations focus on addressing the entire lifecycle of plastics, including production, design, and disposal.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)**
 
 
• UNEP is a global authority that sets the environmental agenda and promotes sustainable development.
 
• It plays a key role in organizing INC sessions and facilitating global cooperation on environmental issues.
 
 
 
• **Geneva’s Role in Global Diplomacy**
 
 
• Geneva is home to over 30 international organizations, including the World Health Organization (WHO) and the International Labour Organization (ILO).
 
• The city serves as a hub for environmental and humanitarian negotiations, offering world-class facilities for global discussions.

questions.question: In March 2025, the Indian Parliament passed the Immigration and Foreigners Bill, 2025. Which of the following Acts was specifically repealed by this legislation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Foreigners Act, 1946**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Immigration and Foreigners Bill, 2025, was enacted to modernize and consolidate laws governing **immigration, foreigners, and their regulation in India**.
 
• The legislation specifically repealed **The Foreigners Act, 1946**, which had been the primary legal framework governing the entry, stay, and deportation of foreigners in India for decades.
 
• The Foreigners Act, 1946, was considered outdated and inadequate to address the complexities of contemporary **immigration and border security challenges**.
 
• The new bill aims to establish a more comprehensive and technology-driven approach to **managing immigration and foreigner-related matters**.
 
• The bill introduces provisions for **e-governance, better monitoring of foreign nationals, and streamlined deportation processes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Foreigners Act, 1946:**

 
 
• It was enacted by the British Government to regulate the entry, presence, and departure of foreigners in India.
 
• The Act empowered the government to declare any foreign national as an illegal immigrant and deport them.
 
• The Act also provided for powers to arrest, detain, or restrict the movement of foreigners under certain circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Immigration Challenges in India:**
 
 
• India faces significant immigration challenges, including **illegal migration across porous borders** with neighboring countries like Bangladesh and Myanmar.
 
• The lack of a modern and unified immigration framework has hindered efficient regulation and monitoring of foreign nationals.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Immigration and Foreigners Bill, 2025:**
 
 
• Introduces a centralized database for monitoring the entry and exit of foreign nationals.
 
• Enhances penalties for violation of immigration laws.
 
• Establishes dedicated immigration courts to expedite the resolution of disputes and deportation cases.
 
 
 
• **Related Legislation:**
 
 
• The Emigration Act, 1983, governs the emigration of Indian nationals for overseas employment and remains unaffected by the new bill.
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, deals with the acquisition and termination of Indian citizenship and is also separate from the Immigration and Foreigners Bill.

questions.question: According to Global Debt Report 2025, what was the share of central bank holdings of domestic sovereign bonds in OECD countries in 2024?

__
 
• According to the Global Debt Report 2025, the share of central bank holdings of domestic sovereign bonds in OECD countries in 2024 was **19% (0.19).**
 
• OECD countries represent economically advanced nations, including key players such as the US, UK, Japan, and European Union member states.
 
• The significant holding of domestic sovereign bonds by central banks highlights their role in stabilizing economies and managing fiscal policies.
 
• The increase in central bank holdings has been influenced by quantitative easing policies implemented during economic downturns.
 
• This share underscores the growing reliance on central banks to provide liquidity and maintain economic stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development):**

 
 
• An intergovernmental organization established in 1961 to promote economic progress and global trade.
 
• It consists of 38 member countries, mostly developed economies.
 
• OECD provides a platform for economic analysis and policy recommendations.
 
 
 
• **Domestic Sovereign Bonds:**
 
 
• Sovereign bonds are debt securities issued by governments to finance their expenditures.
 
• Domestic sovereign bonds are denominated in the issuing country’s local currency.
 
• Central banks often purchase these bonds as part of monetary policy measures.
 
 
 
• **Quantitative Easing (QE):**
 
 
• A monetary policy tool used by central banks to inject liquidity into the economy.
 
• Involves large-scale purchases of government bonds and other securities.
 
• Aimed at reducing interest rates and stimulating economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Economic Stability and Liquidity Management:**
 
 
• Central banks play a key role in maintaining economic stability by controlling inflation and managing liquidity.
 
• Purchasing sovereign bonds is one method to ensure adequate liquidity in financial markets.

questions.question: In April 2025, NITI Aayog released a report titled "Automotive Industry – Powering India's Participation in Global Value Chains". What is the primary objective of this report?

options.text: To compare India's automotive policies with those of neighbouring countries
To assess the environmental impact of India's automotive sector
To propose strategies for enhancing India's role in global automotive value chains
To analyse India's automotive export performance over the past decade

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The report by NITI Aayog aims to outline **strategic measures for enhancing India's participation in global automotive value chains**.
 
• It focuses on **aligning India's automotive industry policies** with global standards to boost competitiveness and innovation.
 
• Key areas addressed include **technology adoption, skill development, and fostering collaboration** between stakeholders.
 
• The report emphasizes **strengthening exports, improving supply chain efficiency, and leveraging India's manufacturing capacity**.
 
• Promoting sustainable practices and integrating advanced technologies like **electric vehicles (EVs) and autonomous systems** are highlighted as vital strategies.

• **Global Value Chains (GVCs):**

 
 
• GVCs refer to the international division of production, where different stages of the manufacturing process are carried out in various countries.
 
• Participation in GVCs helps nations integrate into the global economy and enhance their trade competitiveness.
 
 
 
• **India's Automotive Industry:**
 
 
• India is the world's fourth-largest automotive market and a major exporter of vehicles and auto components.
 
• The industry contributes significantly to India's GDP and provides employment to millions of workers.
 
 
 
• **Electric Vehicles (EVs) and Sustainability:**
 
 
• EVs are a critical focus area in India's automotive strategy to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and promote sustainability.

questions.question: In September 2024, the Uniform Code of Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices (UCPMP) 2024 extended its guidelines to which of the following sectors?

__

• The UCPMP aims to regulate and ensure transparency in interactions between pharmaceutical companies and healthcare professionals, now including medical device manufacturers.
 
• The extension of UCPMP to medical device manufacturers highlights the growing importance of ethical considerations in the healthcare and medical device industry.
 
• Under these guidelines, medical device manufacturers are expected to adhere to ethical standards in advertising, promotions, and interactions with healthcare providers.
 
• This move aligns with the government's efforts to strengthen accountability and safeguard patient interests in the healthcare sector.

• **Uniform Code of Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices (UCPMP)**

 
 
• The UCPMP was introduced by the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Government of India, to regulate marketing practices in the pharmaceutical industry.
 
• It seeks to prevent unethical practices such as excessive gifts, inducements, or sponsorships offered to healthcare professionals.
 
• It emphasizes transparency, accountability, and ethical promotional practices in the healthcare sector.

• It promotes fair competition and deters unethical practices within the medical device industry.

questions.question: What is the name of the Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE) drone discussed at the Drone Industry Conclave 2025?

• **TAPAS** is a Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE) unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) in India.

• TAPAS was showcased at the Drone Industry Conclave 2025 as a significant step towards **India's self-reliance in drone technology**.

questions.question: Which bank of India will mark its 90th anniversary in 2025?

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on **April 1, 1935**, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The RBI is India's central bank, responsible for regulating the country's monetary policy, currency issuance, and financial stability.
 
• It initially started its operations in Kolkata but was permanently shifted to **Mumbai in 1937**.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India will complete **90 years of establishment in 2025.**
 
• The RBI's primary functions include controlling inflation, managing foreign exchange, and regulating banks and non-banking financial companies.

• **History of RBI**

 
 
• The RBI was conceptualized based on the recommendations of the **Hilton Young Commission**.
 
• It was initially established as a private entity but was nationalized in **1949**.
 
 
 
• **RBI's Governance Structure**
 
 
• The RBI is governed by a central board of directors, which includes government-appointed officials and experts.
 
• The **Governor of RBI** serves as the chief executive officer and represents the bank.
 
 
 
• **Key Functions of RBI**
 
 
• Formulating and implementing monetary policy to maintain price stability and economic growth.
 
• Issuing and managing India's currency under the **Currency and Coinage Act**.
 
• Regulating and supervising banks and financial institutions to ensure financial stability.
 
• Maintaining foreign exchange reserves and managing exchange rates.
 
 
 
• **Important Milestones**
 
 
• The RBI played a critical role in the economic reforms of 1991 that liberalized India's economy.
 
• In recent years, it has introduced various digital initiatives like the **Unified Payments Interface (UPI)** for promoting financial inclusion.

questions.question: In March 2025, which health milestone was remembered on National Vaccination Day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulse Polio First Dose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **National Vaccination Day** is observed in India on **16th March** every year.
 
• It was initiated to commemorate the first-ever administration of the **Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV)** in India on **16 March 1995**.
 
• The Pulse Polio Immunization (PPI) program was launched in 1995 with the aim of eradicating polio in India by vaccinating all children under the age of five.
 
• The program became one of the most successful vaccination initiatives, leading to **India being declared polio-free by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2014**.
 
• This milestone is remembered annually to raise awareness about the importance of vaccination in preventing diseases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pulse Polio Immunization Program**

 
 
• Launched in **1995 **under the **Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI)**.
 
• It involved administering two drops of the Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV) to children under five, irrespective of their previous vaccination status.
 
• The program focused on high-risk areas and rapid response to polio outbreaks.
 
• It played a crucial role in achieving a polio-free status for India, certified by WHO in 2014.
 
 
 
• **Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI)**
 
 
• A public-private partnership launched in **1988 **with the goal of eradicating polio worldwide.
 
• Key partners include WHO, UNICEF, Rotary International, CDC, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.
 
• Since its launch, the number of polio cases globally has decreased by over 99%.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Vaccination**
 
 
• Vaccination is one of the most effective ways to prevent infectious diseases.
 
• It helps develop immunity by mimicking an infection without causing illness.
 
• Mass vaccination campaigns like Pulse Polio have saved millions of lives worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Eradication of Polio in India**
 
 
• India reported its last polio case in January 2011 in West Bengal.
 
• On** 27 March 2014, WHO certified the Southeast Asia Region, including India**, as polio-free.
 
• India's success was attributed to strong government commitment, community participation, and support from global health organizations.

questions.question: In November 2024, the birth anniversary of the tribal leader Birsa Munda was celebrated as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Janjatiya Gaurav Divas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Janjatiya Gaurav Divas** is observed to commemorate the birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda, a revered leader in India's independence movement.
 
• Birsa Munda, born on **15 November 1875**, played a key role in leading tribal communities against British colonial rule and exploitation in the late 19th century.
 
• The Government of India officially declared **15th November** as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas in 2021 to honor the contributions of tribal leaders and communities to the nation's history and culture.
 
• The day is marked by various events and activities across the country, focusing on tribal heritage, culture, and recognition of their role in India's freedom struggle.
 
• Birsa Munda's legacy is celebrated as a symbol of tribal pride, resilience, and the fight against oppression and injustice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Birsa Munda:**

 
 
• Birsa Munda was a tribal freedom fighter, religious leader, and folk hero from the Munda tribe in present-day Jharkhand.
 
• He led the **Munda Rebellion** (also known as the Ulgulan movement) against the British colonial government and exploitative landlords.
 
• Birsa Munda advocated for the rights of tribal people and sought to protect their land, culture, and identity.
 
• He passed away at the young age of **25 on June 9, 1900**, but his contributions remain deeply impactful.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Tribal Heritage:**
 
 
• India is home to over **700 tribal groups**, each with unique languages, cultures, and traditions.
 
• Tribal communities constitute approximately **8.6% of India's population**, according to the 2011 Census.
 
• Recognizing tribal contributions helps preserve their heritage and promotes inclusivity in national narratives.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Tribal Welfare:**
 
 
• The Ministry of Tribal Affairs oversees programs and schemes aimed at improving the socio-economic conditions of tribal communities.
 
• Key initiatives include the **Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojana**, **Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana**, and the establishment of Eklavya Model Residential Schools.
 
 
 
• **Other Observances:**
 
 
• India celebrates various days to honor freedom fighters and leaders, such as Gandhi Jayanti, Sardar Patel Jayanti, and Ambedkar Jayanti.
 
• Janjatiya Gaurav Divas adds to this list by recognizing the contributions of tribal leaders and their impact on India's history.

questions.question: Which country ranked highest overall in the Climate Change Performance Index 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Denmark**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Denmark **has been consistently leading global climate change rankings due to its strong policies and commitment to **achieving carbon neutrality by 2050.**
 
• The country excels in renewable energy use, particularly wind energy, which contributes significantly to its electricity generation.
 
• Denmark’s ambitious climate policies include the Climate Act, which legally binds the country to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 70% by 2030 (compared to 1990 levels).
 
• Its high ranking in the** Climate Change Performance Index 2025** is attributed to its proactive measures in renewable energy, energy efficiency, and international cooperation on climate issues.
 
• The Climate Change Performance Index evaluates countries based on greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy, energy use, and climate policy, with Denmark scoring high across all categories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI):**

 
 
• The CCPI is an independent monitoring tool used to track the climate protection performance of 60 countries and the European Union.
 
• The index is jointly published by Germanwatch, the NewClimate Institute, and the Climate Action Network (CAN).
 
• It evaluates countries based on four key categories: greenhouse gas emissions (40%), renewable energy (20%), energy use (20%), and climate policy (20%).
 
• The CCPI aims to enhance transparency in international climate politics and encourage countries to adopt stronger climate measures.
 
 
 
• **Denmark's Renewable Energy Leadership:**
 
 
• Denmark is a global leader in wind energy, with wind turbines accounting for over 40% of its electricity production.
 
• The country has invested heavily in offshore wind farms and plans to build artificial energy islands to harness more renewable energy.
 
• Denmark’s energy transition is supported by governmental policies and public-private partnerships in the green energy sector.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement:**
 
 
• An international treaty adopted in 2015 to combat climate change by limiting global warming to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels, aiming for 1.5°C.
 
• Countries are required to submit nationally determined contributions (NDCs) outlining their climate action plans.
 
• Denmark’s commitment to the Paris Agreement is reflected in its ambitious national targets and initiatives to reduce emissions.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Neutrality:**
 
 
• Carbon neutrality, also known as net-zero emissions, refers to achieving a balance between emitted and absorbed greenhouse gases.
 
• Denmark aims to become carbon neutral by 2050, with interim targets like the 70% reduction in emissions by 2030.
 
• The country is adopting technologies such as carbon capture and storage (CCS) and increasing its reliance on renewable energy to meet these goals.

questions.question: What was the Total Fertility Rate (TFR) in India as per the latest National Family Health Survey - 5 (2019-21)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.0**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The** Total Fertility Rate (TFR)** in India as per the **National Family Health Survey - 5 (2019-21)** is **2.0**, which is below the replacement level of fertility (2.1).
 
• This marks a significant **decline from the TFR of** **2.2** reported during **NFHS-4 (2015-16)**.
 
• The TFR decline is an indicator of increasing awareness about family planning and better access to contraceptive methods.
 
• The survey also highlights that **urban areas have a lower TFR (1.6)** compared to rural areas (2.1).
 
• State-specific trends reveal that several states, including Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Punjab, have achieved TFR levels below replacement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Total Fertility Rate (TFR):**

 
 
• TFR is defined as the average number of children a woman would have during her lifetime.
 
• It is a key demographic indicator used to assess population growth and replacement levels.
 
• The replacement level of fertility is generally considered to be **2.1 children per woman**, which ensures stable population levels.
 
 
 
• **National Family Health Survey (NFHS):**
 
 
• NFHS is a nationwide survey conducted by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, in collaboration with the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS).
 
• It provides essential data on health, nutrition, family planning, and demographic indicators.
 
• NFHS surveys play a crucial role in policy formulation and program implementation.
 
 
 
• **Factors influencing TFR:**
 
 
• Improved access to family planning methods and contraceptives.
 
• Better education levels, especially among women.
 
• Economic development and urbanization.
 
• Awareness campaigns and healthcare outreach programs.
 
 
 
• **Implications of a declining TFR:**
 
 
• A declining TFR can lead to an aging population, reducing the workforce over time.
 
• It emphasizes the need for sustainable population policies and economic adjustments.
 
• Balanced demographic shifts are essential for long-term socio-economic stability.

questions.question: In March 2025, NITI Aayog released the 'Future Front: Quarterly Frontier Tech Insights' report. What is the primary focus of this report?

• Leading companies like IBM, Google, and Microsoft are developing cutting-edge quantum computing systems.

questions.question: What is the target length for the development of a national highway network in India by 2025?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Government of India has set a target to develop a **2 lakh km national highway network** by 2025 under its infrastructure development plan.
 
• The initiative is part of the **Bharatmala Pariyojana**, launched to improve road connectivity across India.
 
• It aims to enhance the efficiency of freight and passenger movement through the development of economic corridors, inter-corridors, feeder routes, and border roads.
 
• This ambitious project focuses on reducing travel time, fuel consumption, and logistics costs, contributing to India's economic growth.
 
• The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) is overseeing the implementation of this target.

• **Bharatmala Pariyojana:**

 
 
• Bharatmala Pariyojana is a** centrally-sponsored road and highway development initiative launched in 2017**.
 
• The scheme focuses on building a robust highway infrastructure, including economic corridors, rural roads, and expressways.
 
• A budget of approximately ₹5.35 lakh crore was allocated for the first phase of Bharatmala Pariyojana.
 
• The program is expected to cover around 34,800 km of roads in Phase I.
 
 
 
• **Economic Corridors:**
 
 
• Economic corridors are routes designed to facilitate efficient movement of goods and services across regions.
 
• They link production centers, markets, and ports to boost trade and industrial growth.
 
• The development of such corridors under Bharatmala aims to reduce logistics costs and enhance supply chain efficiency.
 
 
 
• **National Highway Authority of India (NHAI):**

• It plays a pivotal role in implementing large-scale highway projects, including Bharatmala Pariyojana.
 
• NHAI uses innovative financing methods, such as toll-operate-transfer (TOT) and hybrid annuity models, to fund infrastructure projects.
 
 
 
• **Future Impacts:**

• It is expected to boost tourism, trade, and industrial growth across the country.
 
• The project will create thousands of jobs and contribute to India's GDP growth.

questions.question: During the 2025 demonstration, which types of drones were successfully destroyed by DRDO’s DEW Mk-II(A)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fixed-wing UAVs and Swarm drones**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) successfully demonstrated the **Directed Energy Weapon (DEW) Mk-II(A)** during trials in 2025.
 
• The DEW Mk-II(A) effectively neutralized **Fixed-wing Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Swarm drones**, showcasing its operational capabilities against advanced aerial threats.
 
• The system employs **laser-based technology** to disable or destroy aerial targets by disrupting their onboard electronics or structure.
 
• These trials highlighted India’s advancements in **non-kinetic warfare technologies**, positioning DRDO among the global leaders in Directed Energy Weapons development.
 
• The DEW Mk-II(A) was specifically designed to counter **emerging threats from drones**, which are increasingly being used in military and surveillance applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directed Energy Weapons (DEWs):**

 
 
• DEWs are a class of weapons that emit energy in a focused direction to damage or disable targets.
 
• Common types of DEWs include **laser weapons, microwave weapons, and particle beam weapons**.
 
• They offer advantages such as precision targeting, minimal collateral damage, and low operational costs once deployed.
 
 
 
• **Fixed-wing UAVs:**
 
 
• Fixed-wing UAVs are unmanned aerial systems that use wings like traditional airplanes for flight.
 
• They are commonly used for **surveillance, reconnaissance, and delivery applications** due to their long flight range and efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Swarm Drones:**
 
 
• Swarm drones refer to a coordinated group of drones that operate together to achieve a common objective.
 
• These are often used for **military operations, search-and-rescue missions, and surveillance**.
 
• Swarm drones leverage **artificial intelligence and communication systems** to coordinate their movements.
 
 
 
• **India’s DEW Program:**
 
 
• India has been developing Directed Energy Weapons under DRDO’s Advanced Weapons and Technology program.
 
• These systems are part of the country’s effort to counter modern threats like drones, missiles, and other aerial platforms.
 
 
 
• **Global DEW Development:**
 
 
• Countries such as the USA, China, and Russia are actively developing DEWs for military applications.
 
• These weapons are considered **critical for next-generation warfare** due to their ability to neutralize high-speed and agile threats.

__
 
• **Sunita Williams**, a NASA astronaut of Indian origin, has spent a cumulative **608 days in space** over the course of her missions.
 
• She held the record for the most spaceflight time by a woman until it was surpassed by Peggy Whitson in 2017.
 
• Her most recent mission aboard a SpaceX capsule concluded in **March 2025**, marking her return to Earth.
 
• Sunita Williams has participated in two long-duration missions aboard the International Space Station (ISS), namely Expeditions 14/15 and 32/33.
 
• She is one of the most experienced astronauts in NASA's history and has conducted seven spacewalks totaling 50 hours and 40 minutes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SpaceX Crew Dragon:**

 
 
• SpaceX's Crew Dragon is a spacecraft designed to transport astronauts to and from the ISS.
 
• It is part of NASA's Commercial Crew Program, which aims to enable private companies to provide human spaceflight services.
 
• Sunita Williams was part of one of the Crew Dragon missions, showcasing advancements in commercial spaceflight.
 
 
 
• **International Space Station (ISS):**
 
 
• The ISS is a modular space station in low Earth orbit, serving as a laboratory for scientific research and international collaboration.
 
• It has been continuously inhabited since November 2000, with astronauts from various countries contributing to its operations.
 
• Sunita Williams' missions aboard the ISS focused on scientific experiments, maintenance, and outreach activities.
 
 
 
• **Spacewalks:**
 
 
• A spacewalk, or Extravehicular Activity (EVA), is when an astronaut exits a spacecraft to work in space.
 
• Sunita Williams has performed seven spacewalks, placing her among the most experienced astronauts in this domain.
 
• Her spacewalks include tasks such as repairing equipment and installing components on the ISS.
 
 
 
• **NASA's Human Spaceflight Program:**
 
 
• NASA has been at the forefront of human space exploration since the Apollo program in the 1960s.
 
• Programs such as the Space Shuttle, ISS, and Artemis are key milestones in NASA's efforts to explore space.
 
• Sunita Williams' contributions to human spaceflight have been a significant part of NASA's achievements.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements accurately reflect the outcomes of the 2024 Jammu and Kashmir Assembly elections?

 1. The Congress-JKNC alliance secured a majority with 48 seats.

2. The BJP emerged as the single largest party with 29 seats.

3. Voter turnout was recorded at 63.88%, showing a significant rise compared to the recently concluded Lok Sabha election.

4. The newly elected assembly holds full legislative powers equivalent to other Indian states.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The** Congress-Jammu and Kashmir National Conference (JKNC) alliance secured a majority with 48 seats**, making them the key power holders in the 2024 Assembly elections.
 
• Voter turnout in the 2024 Jammu and Kashmir Assembly elections was recorded at 63.88%, reflecting a significant increase compared to the voter turnout in the most recent Lok Sabha elections.
 
• The BJP did not emerge as the single largest party, as the Congress-JKNC alliance surpassed its seat count.
 
• The newly elected assembly in Jammu and Kashmir does not hold full legislative powers equivalent to other Indian states, as Jammu and Kashmir remains a Union Territory after the abrogation of Article 370 in August 2019.
 
• Statements 1 and 3 are correct, accurately reflecting the outcomes of the 2024 elections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jammu and Kashmir Assembly:** After the abrogation of Article 370 in 2019, Jammu and Kashmir was reorganized into two Union Territories: Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.
 
• **Congress-JKNC Alliance:** Historically, both parties have played significant roles in the political landscape of Jammu and Kashmir, often aligning to counter BJP influence in the region.
 
• **Voter Turnout Trends:** An increase in voter turnout signifies heightened political engagement and interest among citizens, often influenced by key local and national issues.
 
• **BJP Performance:** The BJP has historically aimed to expand its influence in Jammu and Kashmir, but in the 2024 Assembly elections, it fell short in securing a majority.
 
• **Union Territory Status:** Jammu and Kashmir continues to function under a Union Territory framework, meaning its legislative assembly has limited powers compared to full-fledged states like Maharashtra or Tamil Nadu.
